::: {#exm-extended-transition}
#### Unfolding the extended transition function

For the door (@exm-door-machine), the recursive rule of @def-extended-transition peels off the last input three times:

$$
\ba
\delta^*(\text{closed}, \mathtt{lou})
&= \delta\paren{\delta^*(\text{closed}, \mathtt{lo}), \mathtt{u}}
\\&= \delta\paren{\delta\paren{\delta^*(\text{closed}, \mathtt{l}), \mathtt{o}}, \mathtt{u}}
\\&= \delta\paren{\delta\paren{\delta\paren{\delta^*(\text{closed}, \lambda), \mathtt{l}}, \mathtt{o}}, \mathtt{u}}.
\ea
$$

The base case gives $\delta^*(\text{closed}, \lambda) = \text{closed}$,
and then evaluating from the inside out,

$$
\ba
\delta\paren{\delta\paren{\delta(\text{closed}, \mathtt{l}), \mathtt{o}}, \mathtt{u}}
&= \delta\paren{\delta(\text{locked}, \mathtt{o}), \mathtt{u}}
\\&= \delta(\text{locked}, \mathtt{u})
\\&= \text{closed}.
\ea
$$

So $\delta^*(\text{closed}, \mathtt{lou}) = \text{closed}$.

:::
